item.title: Why hasn't Sweden joined the euro and will it ever happen?
item.description: Despite joining the EU in 1994, Sweden still hasn’t joined the euro. Why is this, and could it ever happen in the future?

item.title: What do we know about the Sweden Democrat MP under investigation for drunk driving?
item.description: SD Member of Parliament Katja Nyberg, a former police officer who has been the party spokesperson for police issues, was stopped for suspected drunk driving over the holidays. Blood tests have now come back positive for both alcohol and narcotics.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: vagn
item.description: This word of the day translates easily to English as ‘wagon’, but its wide use in compound words makes it a great Swedish word to have in your vocabulary.

item.title: Sweden denies Turkey request to hear journalist facing terror charges
item.description: Sweden's government said on Thursday that it was denying a request from Turkey for a Swedish court to interrogate a journalist facing terror charges in Turkey.

item.title: EU announces plan to extend 90-day rule for certain non-EU workers
item.description: The European Commission has announced it will look into allowing certain non-EU professionals to stay in the EU beyond the current 90/180-day rule, as part of a future overhaul of its visa system. It also asked EU countries to make visa access "simpler and faster" for skilled workers.

item.title: Global crisis? Step forward Sweden's straight-shooting influencer-in-chief
item.description: The old order is gone, we're in the middle of a rupture, and world leaders are concluding they can't tip-toe around Trump any longer. This has opened the door for one Swedish politician who has made Instagram-friendly plain-speaking an art.

item.title: Q&A: 'We need an agency to bring cutting-edge global expertise to Sweden'
item.description: Sweden's Labour Minister Johan Britz, who represents the Liberal Party, recently called for a new government agency to be launched in Sweden that will take over responsibility for work permits from the Migration Agency. He explains why.

item.title: 'Betrayed': How layoffs at Ericsson's Swedish offices are affecting our readers
item.description: In a recent survey we asked readers working at Ericsson how the recent news of yet another round of layoffs ‒ the third in as many years ‒ is affecting them. Here's what they said.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: varuberg
item.description: Understanding this peculiar word will help you to avoid accidentally alienating people in Sweden.

item.title: Sweden's government asks Migration Agency to propose exemptions to work permit law
item.description: Sweden's government has ordered the Migration Agency to draw up a list of in demand professions which will be exempted from the new higher salary requirement set to come into force later this year.
